title: 1.2 The Scientific Method
description: Steps of the scientific method and experimental design

questions.question: What is the first step of the scientific method?
questions.correctAnswer: Making an observation

questions.question: After making an observation, what is the next step in the scientific method?
questions.correctAnswer: Asking a question

questions.question: What is a hypothesis?
options: A testable explanation or prediction for an observation
questions.correctAnswer: A testable explanation or prediction for an observation

questions.question: After forming a hypothesis, what is the next step in the scientific method?
options: Conducting an experiment to test the hypothesis
questions.correctAnswer: Conducting an experiment to test the hypothesis

questions.question: What is a controlled experiment?
options: An experiment where all variables are changed
An experiment where only one variable is changed at a time while others are kept constant
An experiment conducted without any measurements
An experiment that does not require a hypothesis
questions.correctAnswer: An experiment where only one variable is changed at a time while others are kept constant

questions.question: In a controlled experiment, what is the variable that is changed by the scientist called?
questions.correctAnswer: Independent variable

questions.question: In a controlled experiment, what is the variable that is measured or observed called?
questions.correctAnswer: Dependent variable

questions.question: What are variables that are kept the same in both the experimental and control groups called?
questions.correctAnswer: Controlled variables or constants

questions.question: What is the purpose of a control group in an experiment?
options: To provide a baseline for comparison
questions.correctAnswer: To provide a baseline for comparison

questions.question: After conducting an experiment and analyzing the data, what is the next step in the scientific method?
questions.correctAnswer: Drawing a conclusion

questions.question: What does a conclusion in the scientific method do?
options: States whether the hypothesis is supported or rejected based on the evidence
questions.correctAnswer: States whether the hypothesis is supported or rejected based on the evidence

questions.question: What is the final step of the scientific method?
questions.correctAnswer: Communicating the results to others

questions.question: How can scientific results be communicated?
options: Through scientific journals, conferences, and presentations
questions.correctAnswer: Through scientific journals, conferences, and presentations

questions.question: Why is it important for a hypothesis to be testable?
options: So it can be proven true without evidence
So it can be supported or rejected through experimentation
So it can be published immediately
questions.correctAnswer: So it can be supported or rejected through experimentation

questions.question: What happens to a hypothesis that is repeatedly supported by experiments?
questions.correctAnswer: It becomes a scientific theory

questions.question: What is the difference between a hypothesis and a theory?
options: A hypothesis is a proven fact, while a theory is a guess
A hypothesis is a testable prediction, while a theory is a well-supported explanation supported by extensive evidence
A theory is a prediction, while a hypothesis is an explanation
questions.correctAnswer: A hypothesis is a testable prediction, while a theory is a well-supported explanation supported by extensive evidence

questions.question: What is a scientific law?
options: A well-supported explanation of natural phenomena
A statement that describes a consistent and universal natural phenomenon
A prediction made by a scientist
questions.correctAnswer: A statement that describes a consistent and universal natural phenomenon

questions.question: If a hypothesis is rejected after an experiment, what should the scientist do?
options: Modify the hypothesis and test again
Publish the results as a theory
questions.correctAnswer: Modify the hypothesis and test again

questions.question: Why is replication important in scientific experiments?
options: To make the experiment more expensive
To ensure the results are reliable and consistent
To make the experiment take longer
questions.correctAnswer: To ensure the results are reliable and consistent

questions.question: What is the role of a control group in a plant growth experiment testing a new fertilizer?
options: Plants that receive the new fertilizer
Plants that receive twice the normal amount of fertilizer
questions.correctAnswer: Plants that receive no fertilizer

questions.question: In an experiment testing the effect of light on plant growth, what is the independent variable?
options: The amount of water given to the plants
The amount of light the plants receive
questions.correctAnswer: The amount of light the plants receive

questions.question: In an experiment testing the effect of light on plant growth, what is the dependent variable?
options: The growth or height of the plant
questions.correctAnswer: The growth or height of the plant

questions.question: What is data collected during an experiment?
options: The information and measurements gathered from observations
The question asked at the beginning
questions.correctAnswer: The information and measurements gathered from observations

questions.question: What is the purpose of analyzing data after an experiment?
options: To identify patterns and determine whether the data supports the hypothesis
questions.correctAnswer: To identify patterns and determine whether the data supports the hypothesis

questions.question: What is an experimental group in a controlled experiment?
options: The group that does not receive the treatment
The group that receives the treatment or has the independent variable applied
The group where no measurements are taken
The group that forms the hypothesis
questions.correctAnswer: The group that receives the treatment or has the independent variable applied

questions.question: Why is it important to change only one variable at a time in an experiment?
options: To be certain that the observed effect is caused by the independent variable
To reduce the cost of the experiment
questions.correctAnswer: To be certain that the observed effect is caused by the independent variable

questions.question: What is the role of peer review in the scientific method?
options: To evaluate the quality and validity of research before publication
questions.correctAnswer: To evaluate the quality and validity of research before publication

questions.question: Observations made using the five senses or with instruments are referred to as what?
questions.correctAnswer: Qualitative and quantitative data

questions.question: What type of data involves numerical measurements such as height, mass, and temperature?
questions.correctAnswer: Quantitative data

questions.question: What type of data involves descriptions using words such as color, texture, and smell?
questions.correctAnswer: Qualitative data
